item.title: Atomic magnetism reveals why iron, but not chromium, can produce ammonia using sunlight
item.description: Two nearly identical materials have completely different chemical behavior. Research teams at the University of Vienna and TU Wien studied catalysts that use the energy of sunlight to produce ammonia. Surprisingly, when the three iron atoms that form tiny triangles in these catalysts are replaced by chromium atoms, the chemical reaction no longer takes place. Fuente: Phys.org.

Por eso, cuando una administración se propone cambiar su software de oficina, no basta con encontrar una alternativa que haga más o menos lo mismo. item.title: Molecular architecture determines tomato plant resistance to its main pest
item.description: An international study investigating why wild tomatoes are more resistant to the tomato leafminer (Phthorimaea absoluta) than cultivated varieties revealed that the secret lies in the spatial structure of a plant defense molecule. The researchers mapped the biochemical origin of this difference and demonstrated that altering four amino acids in a single enzyme is sufficient to alter the structure of the substance and increase its toxicity against the pest. This finding paves the way for creating resistant tomatoes through gene editing. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Explaining the difference between brittle and ductile behavior in polymer glasses
item.description: Glasses are (mostly) brittle, metals can be ductile (plastic), and liquids flow easily. Polymers are interesting because they exhibit all three types of behavior, depending on their chemical nature, temperature, and deformation rate. If polymers are not able to crystallize, their low-temperature state is glassy, and they are hard and transparent. One example is poly(methylmethacrylate) [PMMA], which has been used as an artificial glass since the early 20th century. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Chornobyl dog population shows genetic signatures of directional selection
item.description: The latest research on the wild population of dogs in Chornobyl reveals that the genetic differences between these dogs and other similarly isolated dog populations are likely evidence of directional selection, not mutation. The work suggests a potential association between genetic selection and environmental variables and could advance understanding of local adaptation and genomic resilience in contaminated environments. The study appears in Genes. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Same radical, different paths: X-ray snapshots reveal how neighboring molecules shape its movement
item.description: Chemical reactions have their own "impatient molecules." Unable to stay still even for a moment, they latch onto other molecules indiscriminately. Researchers have now found that even these molecules change where they "sit" and how far they roam depending on who their neighbors are. The findings are expected to help scientists make better medicines and materials by directing reactions only to the desired sites. Fuente: Phys.org.
